plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch-adjusted design
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 12-sample bulk RNA-seq (salmon-quantified, 12000 genes) kidney experiment with 6 treated vs 6 control samples processed in two known batches, each batch balanced across both conditions. Because the batch is balanced (holds both conditions), it is added as a fixed-effect covariate in the DESeq2 design (~batch + condition) rather than corrected in the counts themselves, preserving the count model's mean-variance structure while removing batch-driven variance from the residual and increasing power for the condition test. The workflow: (1) QC sample structure via blind VST, PCA, and sample-distance heatmap colored by both condition and batch to confirm no unexpected structure or outliers before modeling; (2) minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smaller group size); (3) DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization inside the model (no pre-normalized counts); (4) model with explicit reference levels and named contrast (condition: treated vs control, adjusting for batch); (5) DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage of the condition log2 fold change, reporting shrunken and unshrunken LFC, SE, and flagging Cook's-distance count outliers (NA p-values expected given n=6 per batch cell); (6) Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, inspecting the p-value histogram as a diagnostic; (7) functional enrichment via over-representation analysis with an explicit tested-gene universe against MSigDB Hallmark (human) and Reactome (human-filtered) gene sets, falling back to preranked fgsea on the Wald statistic only if the significant gene list is very small (<50 genes, since ORA has no power there); (8) a consolidated report with fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene set collection versions, seeds), and explicit thresholds/gene counts at every stage. Enrichment gene-set references (MSigDB Hallmark human, Reactome pathways) and the organism annotation package (org.Hs.eg.db) are confirmed present in the environment.
